unit.why: A compilation note on tefillin and constant intention, with a testimony about the Seer of Lublin's yihudim, frames a short first-person memorate by the Zhidachov rebbe: heavenly voices praise him after prayer in tefillin, then cry woe when he handles his pipe without intention.
unit.boundary_note: part of a running tefillin compilation; previous and next divisions continue the same homiletic/halakhic thread

stories.start_quote: ופ״א אמר מורי דודי הקדוש מזדיטשוב
stories.end_quote: ושמעתי קורין ווי לפלניא דמריד במאריה
stories.summary_en: The Zhidachov rebbe recounts that, going to prayer in radiant tefillin, he heard heaven proclaim honour before him, and after moving his pipe without intention he heard a cry of woe against one who rebels against his Master; the text uses this to teach that every act must be done for God's sake.
